_source: Rules are client-dictated or vault-verified. Each carries where it came from. Do not add a rule here on a hunch - an over-broad rule that cries wolf gets the whole sweep ignored.

rules.name: 'no trip charge' / unpaired offer wording
rules.pattern: no trip charge|no service fee|free visit
rules._why: Client text 2026-08-22: 'Let's NOT say no Service fee please, let's say no trip fee (FREE ESTIMATE)'. The phrase never appears alone. Was on 31 of 54 pages until 2026-08-25.

rules.name: free-first-visit framing
rules._why: The free safety inspection happens AFTER the work. Never framed as a free first visit. He charges to diagnose.

rules.name: forbidden diagnostic price
rules._why: pricing-approved-2026-08-24.md - the $349/$350 diagnostic is never published, anywhere.

rules.name: tax-credit figure published (check tense AND brief)
rules.pattern: may cover up to 30%|30% of (the cost|installation)|up to \$1,000[^.]{0,60}(charger|30C)
rules._why: Section 30C terminated for property placed in service after 2026-06-30 (P.L. 119-21). WARN not BLOCK because this pattern cannot tell 'may cover 30%' (false, blocking) from 'previously covered 30%, expired June 30 2026' (true, past tense). Three EV city pages quote the percentage in correct past tense as of 2026-08-25 - the EV brief says no figure at all, so it is an open judgement call, not a defect. READ EACH HIT.

rules.name: legal address published
rules._why: Public NAP is 9488 Fairfax Blvd. The legal address is never published.

rules.name: 'LLC' in public copy
rules._why: Client instruction: never 'LLC' in public-facing copy.

rules.name: named competitor
rules._why: Competitors are never named on the site.

rules.name: thermography certification implied
rules._why: He owns and uses a thermal camera. That is the claim. Never a certification.

rules.name: hand-typed review count (CR-200)
rules._why: Should render via [ev_review_count]/[ev_review_rating], never a typed number. 55 pages hand-type it today; one said 91 while the rest said 105. Until the shortcodes are registered this reports the scale of the debt, not a new defect.

rules.name: unrendered shortcode leaking to readers
rules._why: If this fires, the shortcode is in the copy but not registered - readers see literal brackets. Worse than the hardcoded number.

rules.name: response-time / availability promise
rules.pattern: (?:we|our team|ahmad|he)\s+(?:\w+\s+){0,4}(?:respond|response|arrive|get there|be there|show up)\s+(?:within|in under|in less than)(?!\s+one\s+business\s+day)|(?:we|our|us)\b[^.]{0,50}\bwithin \d+ hours?|available most days|right away[^.]{0,30}(?:call|service|arrive)|we(?:'ll| will) be there|immediate(?:ly)? availab|(?:we|our)\s+(?:\w+\s+){0,3}promptly
rules._why: Bans a SPECIFIC GUARANTEED WINDOW the business has not committed to - 'within 2 hours', 'we'll be there', 'immediately available'. *** CARVE-OUT ADDED 2026-08-26, OPERATOR DECISION: 'We respond within one business day' is NOT banned. It is true, the client responds to emergencies, and he wants to keep it. It is live on ~36 pages as a sitewide template string and it stays. Do NOT strip it from drafts and do NOT open a backwards sweep for it. The regex now carries a negative lookahead for exactly that phrase. *** The earlier note calling it unvalidated was wrong; it has since been validated with the client. Same-day and emergency availability was never banned either - it is the client's strongest and most under-marketed service, with a Google review on file. Must NOT fire on urgency ratings addressed to the homeowner ('stop using the circuit and call now', 'needs same-day attention') - those are correct and required. The distinction: an invented guaranteed turnaround is banned; one-business-day response, same-day/emergency capability, and how fast the reader should act are all allowed. *** 2026-08-26: scoped 'within N hours' to require a first-person subject within 50 chars. It was firing on 'If it trips again within 24 hours, stop resetting and call an electrician' - a homeowner urgency instruction the rule explicitly must not flag. ***

rules.name: detection-rate or savings figure
rules._why: Brief LAYER 2 §2.2 bans detection-rate and savings figures. No source data supports a specific percentage for fault detection or dollar amount for savings. These are unfalsifiable marketing claims.

rules.name: certification not held (extends thermography rule)
rules._why: Brief LAYER 2 §2.2 bans implying certifications not held. The thermography camera is OWNED, not a certification. The only held certification is VA DPOR Master Electrician #2710086216. Any 'certified'/'accredited' claim must reference the DPOR licence specifically; blanket statements are banned. This extends the existing thermography-specific rule to cover the general case.

rules.name: permit exemption asserted that the County does not publish (CR-233)
rules.pattern: Like-for-Like Replacement = Generally No Permit|no electrical permit needed in most cases|like-for-like[^.]{0,60}generally do not require a permit|no permit needed
rules._why: Fairfax County publishes NO like-for-like exemption. Verified 2026-08-25 against two County pages: permit-library/electrical-residential requires a permit for 'replacement of electrical equipment or fixtures'; when-permit-required requires one for 'New, repair or relocated electrical fixtures' and exempts only low-voltage (50V max) systems. Do NOT swing to the opposite overclaim either - the County's wording does not support asserting a permit IS required for a specific job. Correct form: state the absence of a published exemption and that the position is established for the address before work starts.

_lifted_rules.original_reason: plans/_HANDOFF-track-c-2026-08-24.md line 134 - 'He did not know the term.'
_lifted_rules.why_it_was_wrong: Not recognising a trade term is a vocabulary gap, not a capability gap. The rule was inferred from a vocabulary observation and then enforced as a capability limit for four days. Live copy on /whole-house-rewire-fairfax-va/ and /electrical-troubleshooting/ was correct the whole time.
_lifted_rules.do_not_reinstate_without: a direct statement from the client that he does NOT do this work
